conflictsRaised: C1 — smm_bot authority hole (verified, not inferred). Six of the eight callback handlers in smm_bot/bot.py carry no is_admin check: generate: (:843), copy: (:881), schedule: (:897), approve: (:961), reject: (:982), edit: (:992). Only togglefeat: (:221) and setmodel: (:231) are guarded. The sharpest case is approve: — I read bot.py:961-980 and it performs NO principal check before calling publish_to_all, which fans out to Telegram channel, Telegram group, VKontakte, Instagram and TikTok. The only barrier is that Telegram delivers a callback query solely from a message carrying the keyboard, i.e. a channel-delivery property, not an authority check — the exact failure mode named by 'CHANNEL IDENTITY != BUSINESS AUTHORITY' and 'BUTTON != AUTHORITY'. The FSM text handlers /done (:402), bulk_distribute (:455) and the manual scheduling flow (:725, :732, :741) are likewise unguarded. Not resolved here: this is a live production security finding in a bot that is out of scope for the UX cycle, and it needs an owner decision about who fixes it and when.

C2 — VKontakte exists in live code and live copy, against CLAUDE.md rule 7 («VK/MAX-ссылок в проекте быть не должно»). Three independent instances, all verified: (1) smm_bot/publishers.py:32-33 gates a VK publish target on VK_TOKEN + VK_GROUP_ID and calls api.vk.com/method/wall.post at :125 and :218; (2) api-proxy.sanitized.php L187-211 exposes live, routable vk_auth and vk_sdk_auth login routes under the comment «НОВОЕ: Вход через VK ID»; (3) the fenced SMS arm at L181-185 still tells the reader that login is «только ВКонтакте / Telegram», so the policy conflict is in user-adjacent copy as well as in code. Reported, not resolved: whether the rule or the code is wrong is the owner's call. NOTE on blast radius — if VK is removed, (2) and (3) are AUTHORITY changes requiring negative tests, not UX edits, and (1) removes one of smm_bot's five publish targets.

C3 — the public marketing site's scope is undeclared, and three untriaged surfaces depend on the answer. The architecture document scopes the programme to the chat-first shell but never states whether the public site is inside it. Three user-facing anonymous surfaces sit there: the YClients booking deep-link in index.html (5 occurrences, all off-domain), the community UI deployed as a Next.js chunk on muzhskayaestetika.рф (no source in this repository), and the anonymous guest chat with MAYA (live backend, no front-end found in index.html). A fourth complication: index.html also carries an authenticated client cabinet (cabinet_session) rendering visit history, loyalty balance, subscription and upcoming visit — i.e. the public site duplicates PWA surfaces already dispositioned elsewhere. I classified all of these OUT OF SCOPE for the chat-first UX because the page they live on has no chat and no session to bind an intent to, but that is a reading of scope, not a decision. Owner decision needed; it plausibly belongs beside D10 (bundle strategy).

C4 — source-of-truth gap: seven of the 135 rows rest on production evidence that is absent from this checkout, so every statement about them describes an artefact nobody in this cycle can read. site_guest_chat.py (evidenced by a production inventory), site_publications.py (evidenced by a production sha256, 321 lines), the real api-proxy.php (only a sanitized test fixture exists; `find . -name 'api-proxy*.php'` returns nothing else), webhook_server.py community/guest wiring (`grep -c "api/site"` returns 0 here while production is said to run the modules), the guest-chat front-end (proven absent from index.html but plausibly deployed like the Next.js community chunk), tg-config.php and api-proxy.codex-loyalty-20260721.php (both known only through package5-exhaustive-edge.json). Worst case: site_publication_bot.py, where `grep -rn site_publication_bot` over the whole repository returns ZERO matches — it is a filename with no code behind it. Per 'UNKNOWN is never rendered as failure' I recorded these as unresolved-in-this-checkout, never as retired. Resolving them requires reading the production host, which this cycle's fence forbids, so it needs an explicit owner instruction.

C5 — a stale duplicate of the entire front proxy is live at a second public URL. package5-exhaustive-edge.json records app/api-proxy.codex-loyalty-20260721.php on muzhskayaestetika.рф, 146896 bytes, 92 phpActions — a July-2026 snapshot of the whole identity + panel + god surface, bypassing any hardening applied to api-proxy.php after 2026-07-21. I classified it OUT OF SCOPE because it is not a UX decision, and that explicitly does NOT mean leave it there: it is an AUTHORITY/ops removal that needs no parity proof, since it duplicates a live surface by construction. Raising it rather than acting, per the read-only fence.

C6 — the realtime voice PII boundary diverges from the bot's own baseline, against CLAUDE.md gotcha 4. realtime_bridge.py applies redact_pii on the LLM path only: the raw transcript goes to the client and to logs, and raw audio goes to OpenAI unconditionally. The bot's handle_voice (bot.py:2379-2397) is stricter — it refuses audio outright while a contact-collection flow is in the consent/name/phone/confirm stages. That is a divergence in the 152-FZ contour and a direct hit on gate G5, which requires all five client-preview fences to fire independently. Voice is FENCED today, which is the only reason this is not currently exposed. It must be resolved before voice is unfenced; it is a security-track finding, not a design choice available to the widget contract.

C7 — excluding smm_bot changes a published primary-navigation number. All 11 of smm_bot's primary-nav entries are in this untriaged set, and I classified them out of scope because they are primary navigation of a different product. Consequence, verified by re-joining the inventory: MAYA's own primary-nav census is 101 entry points, not 112. None of the 20 primary-nav rows already dispositioned RETIRE FROM PRIMARY NAVIGATION lies in smm-bot (they are pwa 15, telegram-bot 4, web-public 1), so no part of the retirement plan depends on the exclusion — but §3.3 and §7.2 of the architecture document should be restated against 101 so nobody later reads the smm_bot commands as MAYA navigation that failed to be retired. (Separately: my name-join yields 20 such rows where §3.2 reports 19; the gap is attributable to the three duplicate surface names and is not load-bearing.)

C8 — the scheduler channel double-counts smm_bot by construction, and the 9 renamed rows double-count the native bridge. Three rows appear in both the scheduler channel and the smm-bot channel (scheduler_loop, queue_health_loop, holiday_loop) — the same three loops seen from two inventory angles; I classified both copies identically so no capability is silently dropped, but the census should collapse them. Separately, the nine dispositions that §3.2 already reports as unmatched are not orphans: they are near-duplicate NAMES of untriaged rows 0-8 (the booking deep-link and the eight native-shell plugins), each already carrying a round-1/round-2 disposition. I honoured those prior adjudications rather than re-deciding them — KEEP AS CAPABILITY → out of scope or chat-native, SECURITY/AUTHORITY ONLY → settings/security, MOVE INTO CHAT WIDGET → convert to widget, MERGE → retire after parity — but the two name variants must be reconciled to one row each before anyone can claim 795/795 without an asterisk.
